My experience. Writing after a week from discharge.
++ Visited this hospital for first time in my life.

Location: 5minutes away from Borivali W railway station. Landmark: Diamond Talkies, Lokmanya Tilak / LT Road. From LT Road, there is a small lane - 1 car can pass at a time next to Benzer readmade clothes shop. Go inside the small lane. Left hand side you will see Purohit hospital and right hand side you will see residential building. Take left lane to reach hospital.

++ Had been hospitalized due to COVID for 10days.
++ Dedicated COVID center.
++ Patients are NOT allowed to roam inside and outside hospital premise.
++ Families are NOT allowed to visit dedicated COVID center room area. Only reception area is allowed.
++ Ground floor and first floor with beds.
++ Great services by nurses viz.; experienced nurses, prompt room service when alarmed using WiFi device kept next to patient beds, timely reminder and feed of medicines, routinely check-up from morning till night 10pm, nurse shifts changes 3 times a day (24 hours).
++ Packaged breakfast in morning with tea/coffee, Packaged lunch, Packaged breakfast in evening with tea / coffee and packaged Dinner given to COVID patients. Being a foodie, the packaged food was of Quality, quantity, protein, nutritious and it was delicious. Believe me. Everyday it taste great with variety of menu's.
++ Have heard, foods from hotel can be ordered and delivered to patient by clerks. I never need to avail that service since packaged food was better.
++ Warm water on request given to patients by clerks.
++ Turmeric Milk given to patients at night.
++ Daily cleaning of rooms by clerks 2 - 3 times a day.
++ Beds are normal. Please do not expect 3 star or 5 star category beds here. Nice beds that gives your back proper rest and it does not pain. i don't have back-pains / slip-dic disease so point to be noted for patients with back-pain.
++ Junior doctor visits twice a day 9am and 7pm answers queries and guides.
++ Main Doctor (MD  Physician) visits twice a day 11:30am and 8:30pm at patient beds and answers queries and guides.
++ For washing clothes, you can ask for cleaner who washes clothes of patients on requests. This is not billed to hospital. patient and cleaner to manage internally and is charged lumsum.
++ Most important, oxygen cylinders are available and given to patients on MD doctor's advice and consultation. Daily morning oxygen cylinders are delivered / exchanged at hospital premises.
++ Remdisiver injections are given to COVID patients on MD doctor advice and on time.
++ During my tenure, the hospital was not fully consumed / less patients 10 patients approx.
++ Total 3 toilets available in hospital. During my tenure, i did not face difficulties and was able to manage myself. Toilets are cleaned twice - thrice a day. there is availability of hot water for bathing.
++ Clean premise. Silent environment. Good ventilation.
++ Small hospital but i appreciate the way they treated to ME!
++ Not that expensive.
++ Treatment was done well.

featured_reviews.name: Durga
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am writing this review as an admitted patient who expected transparency, communication, and basic patient care, but unfortunately my experience raised several concerns.

One of my concerns involved the handling of medical supplies during my admission. I noticed items being taken away from my room and, when questioned, I was informed that these were being collected as replacements for items provided by the hospital. However, this process was never explained to me in advance. As a patient, I believe there should be complete transparency regarding any consumables, IV fluids, or medical supplies being used and accounted for, especially when these may ultimately be reflected in the final bill. I had to proactively raise this concern with the hospital administration myself.

My primary concern, however, was regarding the gastroenterology consultation. Throughout the day, I was repeatedly informed by the nursing staff that the gastroenterologist would be visiting me. Whenever I followed up, I was told that the doctor would come but that no one knew when. Even at around 9:30 PM, I was still waiting for clarity regarding the visit.

When I approached the reception desk for an update, I was informed that the gastroenterologist does not usually visit on Saturdays. This directly contradicted the information I had been receiving throughout the day. When I questioned why conflicting information had been provided, the RMO, Dr. Drishti, intervened in the conversation.

Unfortunately, my interaction with Dr. Drishti was disappointing. I found her communication to be dismissive and lacking empathy towards an admitted patient who was unwell and seeking clarity regarding their treatment. Rather than addressing my concern regarding the contradictory information provided by the staff, I was simply told that the doctor would come and that his timing was not fixed. No clear explanation was provided regarding the consultation process, expected timeline, or next steps. Additionally, at no point did the RMO assess my condition, enquire about my health status, or provide reassurance despite my repeated concerns.

As a patient admitted under medical care, I expected better communication, coordination, and accountability. Patients should not be left waiting for hours without updates, nor should they receive conflicting information from different departments regarding specialist consultations.

I would like to acknowledge that several nurses and staff members were caring and professional, and the facilities themselves were good. However, transparency, communication, accountability, and patient engagement require significant improvement. Patients who are admitted, unwell, and paying for specialist care deserve timely information, clear communication, and respectful treatment.

I am from Chhattisgarh and suddenly developed severe imbalance to the extent that I was unable to stand properly. On the advice of our family neuro physician, we immediately consulted Dr. Arvind Kulkarni, a highly reputed neurosurgeon known to us through successful surgeries of our acquaintances.
After examining me and reviewing my MRI, Dr. Kulkarni advised immediate surgery. We chose Breach Candy Hospital because of its excellent reputation. The surgery was successfully performed on 28th March, and throughout the entire process, we received exceptional care and guidance.
The hospital facilities, especially the Super Deluxe Room arrangements, were outstanding. The nursing staff, paramedical team, and housekeeping staff were extremely caring, courteous, and professional.
Dr. Kulkarni’s counseling, clarity of explanation, patience in answering every query, and reassuring approach before and after surgery were remarkable. I would also especially like to thank Dr. Janardhan, a wonderful doctor and compassionate human being, who closely monitored my recovery and explained every detail with great care and positivity.
Today, I am able to stand on my feet again, and for that, my heartfelt gratitude goes to Dr. Kulkarni, Dr. Janardhan, and the entire team of Breach Candy Hospital. We shall always remain grateful for the excellent treatment and humane care provided to us.

featured_reviews.name: Prakhar Gupta
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely shameful and horrifying experience.

I called the hospital in the middle of the night asking for an ambulance for my father during a medical emergency. Instead of helping, they kept me on hold and slowly kept reciting a phone number to call myself while I was trying to manage my father’s condition.

The hospital was barely 7 minutes away, yet the ambulance took around 30 minutes to arrive at 2 AM. Those minutes matter in an emergency.

And the nightmare did not end there.

After reaching the hospital, there was no stretcher ready, no emergency staff attending immediately, and we literally had to shout for help while bringing in a critical patient.

Most shocking of all, the ambulance did not even have a proper oxygen mask available.

No family should ever have to go through this level of negligence during a life-and-death emergency. A hospital that advertises emergency care should at the very least have a functioning emergency response system, trained staff ready to act, and properly equipped ambulances.

I would strongly urge people to think twice before depending on this hospital in a real emergency situation.
